subject: chains w. mean, sd, and quantiles + what's left

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: chains w. mean, sd, and quantiles + what's left
parts:
I added the mean, sd, and quantiles methods
for parameters within a chain and across chains.

I included methods for calculating multiple quantiles
at once giving a vector of probs (only one sort required).
I also included a utility method for central intervals
returning a std::pair.

REMAINING QUESTION:
This is only for the base parameters, not their squares.
I'm still waiting on Andrew and Matt to chime in here
to see if we're going to need to track ESS, etc. on
higher moments.

REMAINING METHODS:
That only leaves the following more challenging
methods to implement:

- split potential scale redux (aka split R-hat)
- effective sample size (w. variogram estimator)
- autocorrelation
- smallest posterior interval (SPIn)

plus maybe:

- ? potential scale reduction (aka R-hat)
- ? mcmc_error (MCMC error on the mean estimate)

We can do naive implementations of these, but it'd be
nice to start thinking about FFT approaches.

Does anyone know a good way to implement SPIn? Or even
how it's defined for a finite sample set? Are
we going to need to do some density estimation?
I can always look at Doug Bates's implementation for
Coda.

MORE EFFICIENCY on BASICS:
The implementation uses boost::accumulators for the
quantiles. I could also use that package for mean,
sd, other moments, and a few other things. Alas, I
don't see a smallest interval method.

It's using copies that aren't really necessary by
reading all the samples into a vector and then
computing on that. (It's even using the permuted copy
because that's the only way to get all kept samples cross chains
other than getting the chains in order one by one.)

What we can do to make this faster
is implement a visitor (aka map) method that would take
a functor argument and apply it to all the kept samples (without
permutation -- this isn't end-user facing!). The signatures
for within and across chains would be:

template <typename F>
visit_kept(size_t param_index,
F& fun);

template <typename F>
visit_kept(size_t chain_index,
size_t param_index,
F& fun);

The Boost accumulators are nice in that they're implemented
as functors, so I can just pass them in directly.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] chains w. mean, sd, and quantiles + what's left
parts:
Thanks. I found Chen and Shao's ref and read it.
Very simple with MCMC samples.

smallest_posterior_interval(x,p)

1. Sort the samples x[1] ... x[M].

2. Set p-interval width to integer W = round(M * p).

3. Find m that minimizes x[m+W] - x[m].

4. Return (x[m], x[m+W])

There may be ties in 3. It's easiest to just take
the minimum m in that case. Though it might make
more sense graphically to take the most central
in the case of ties.

Given that M * p may not already be round, we
could also do the median-like thing and interpolate
the endpoints. But Chen and Shao just round. With
lots of samples it shouldn't matter much.

There might be a binary-search-like way to cut
down on some calculations, but it's easy enough
to do the exhaustive search in O(n) time in
step 3 -- we're already in for the O(n log n)
sort in step 1.

- Bob
